# http-json

Fetch a JSON URL; return status, top-level keys, selected values, size and the saved body path.

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--url` | str | yes |  | http, https or file URL |
| `--keys` | str | no | `""` | Comma-separated keys to return; dotted paths for nested keys |
| `--timeout` | float | no | `20` | Seconds before the request is abandoned |
| `--method` | enum: GET, HEAD | no | `GET` | HTTP method; read-only methods only |

Run it from the repo root:

```
caveman-blocks run http-json --url <str>
```

It prints one JSON object with the keys status, keys, selected, size, full, truncated.

Without the CLI, `python3 .blocks/http-json.py --url <str>` runs the same file, but nothing is enforced: no effects gate, no path confinement, no output cap.
